title: Janus-Q HGRM architecture as H331 design blueprint
rationale: Janus-Q (arXiv:2602.19919, HKUST 2026) is an end-to-end event-driven LLM trading framework that achieved +102% Sharpe improvement and +17.5% direction accuracy over strong baselines. It treats financial news events as primary decision units (not auxiliary signals), using a Hierarchical Gated Reward Model (HGRM) to align LLM reasoning with multi-objective trading goals. H331 proposes applying FinBERT to M&A announcement 8-K filings to classify deal-break risk — Janus-Q's 10 fine-grained event types and HGRM reward structure are a direct architectural blueprint. Specifically: (1) encode M&A 8-K text with FinBERT, (2) classify into event sub-types (hostile/PE/strategic/cross-border), (3) use HGRM-style reward = f(completion_probability × gross_spread − break_probability × loss_on_break), (4) RL fine-tuning on historical M&A outcomes. This upgrades H331 from a simple FinBERT scorer to a full decision-oriented agent.
